build.summary:
The six course overlays, the plain HTML version and both harness pages are built, but the final code has only been verified outside Next: the shared dev server on port 3000 died at about 14:46 (not my doing) and never came back. Earlier versions of all six overlays and the plain page did render under the real dev server with no console errors. Everything after that was checked in real headless Chrome through a file:// harness I built in the scratchpad (same components, same compiled globals.css and fonts, React StrictMode on).

What exists:
- **Shared section components** (`src/components/course/sections/`): Education, Skills, Career (Star Missions), Certifications, About & Contact, ContactForm, ResumeStarCard. Each renders from `src/content/portfolio.ts` and takes `variant="overlay" | "plain"`; the two looks come from one set of CSS custom properties.
- **CourseOverlay** `{ id, onExit, mission? }`: modal dialog with header band (PaintingThumb, COURSE n, door badge, chunky title, painting title, door accent), scrollable body, footer exit button. Focus moves to the heading, Tab is trapped, Esc calls `onExit` once, focus returns to the opener.
- **Star Missions and coursework cards**: real tab patterns with arrow keys, Home/End and roving tabindex.
- **Certification stars**: a true extruded CSS 3D gold star (front, back and ten shaded rim faces) for completed ones, a slower outlined badge for in-progress ones, both paused under reduced motion.
- **ContactForm**: labels, native validation, aria-live status, button disabled while sending, EmailJS `sendForm` loaded lazily on first submit. Delivery goes through a context so the harnesses use a mock and nothing is ever sent.
- **PlainPortfolio** `{ actions, nameHeadingLevel? }`: no "use client"; skip link, sticky header with nav and actions slot, hero, About, Education, Skills, Experience & Projects, Certifications, navy Contact band, footer, print rules. Anchors #home #about #education #skills #experience #projects #certification #contact all exist; `<main id="plain-portfolio">`.
- **Harnesses**: `/dev/overlays?id=…&mission=…&open=0&send=fail&review=1` and `/dev/plain?send=fail&review=1&h=2`.

contractGaps: CourseOverlayProps gained an optional `mission?: string` (preselects a Star Mission). PlainPortfolioProps gained an optional `nameHeadingLevel?: 1 | 2`. The existing props are unchanged.
globals.css sets `h1…h6 { font-family: Monda }` and a Quicksand body font, unlayered, so they beat Tailwind utilities. Every heading in my module carries a class that sets its font explicitly.
I reference `--font-outfit`, `--font-titan` and `--font-pixel-face` (set on <html> by layout.tsx) directly, because the `@theme inline` font tokens are not guaranteed to be emitted as CSS variables.

The shared `.btn-retro` (cream on royal, about 4.1:1) and `.btn-retro--ruby` (cream on ruby, about 4.3:1) fall just under AA 4.5:1 at 16 px. I override colours locally for my two uses (overlay exit button, plain hero 'Get in touch'); fixing the primitives in globals.css would be better.
PaintingThumb sets width and height inline from its `size` prop; I override with `!important` inside `.cx-frame` so the framed thumbnail can scale responsively.

Environment: a transient 500 on every page from src/app/favicon.ico ('PNG is not in RGBA format') while another module replaced it, then the dev server exited at about 14:46 and no process has listened on port 3000 since. Earlier tsc runs showed errors in src/app/dev/audio/tests.ts and src/game/engine/game.ts (other modules, mid-edit); the final run is clean.
blueprintDeviations: Plain version: missions are grouped as Work experience, Technical labs, Personal projects (résumé order) instead of Star 1–5 order, and the 'Star n · kind' line is left out there. The overlay keeps Star 1–5 as tabs.

Plain version headings: h2 is the conventional label (About, Education, Skills, Certifications, Contact) with the playful course title as an eyebrow; the career section uses 'Experience & Technical Projects' as its h2. 'About & Contact' is split into two nav entries.
Résumé overlay: the exit button reads '[ BACK TO THE LOBBY (ESC) ]' because the pedestal star is not a painting; the five courses use '[ JUMP OUT OF PAINTING (ESC) ]'.
The painting blurb in the overlay header is hidden at 640 px and below, and the whole painting line is hidden when the viewport is under 520 px tall, to keep the reading area.
Coursework cards are a selectable row with a description box underneath (item-menu style, tab semantics) rather than cards that expand in place. The plain version shows all four expanded.
The About overlay also carries the tagline, the one-line summary and a credits strip (copyright, role, Camino Code logo), so every content string is reachable in-game.
LinkedIn and GitHub use generic line icons with text labels, not brand logos.
Content strings intentionally not rendered: SITE_URL, internal ids, the three EmailJS ids (used as sendForm arguments). The form's success and failure messages appear only after a submit.
integrationNotes: Imports are unchanged: `CourseOverlay` from `@/components/course/CourseOverlay` and `PlainPortfolio` from `@/components/course/PlainPortfolio`. GameRoot's existing `<CourseOverlay id={overlay} onExit={commands.exitCourse} />` works as is.

Esc: CourseOverlay listens on `document` in the capture phase and calls stopPropagation. GameRoot's window-capture listener runs first and already returns while an overlay is open, so Esc is handled once.

Focus on close returns to the element that had focus when the overlay opened. If that element is gone (e.g. a pause-menu fast-travel button), it falls back to the first element with `data-overlay-return-focus`. Adding that attribute to a persistent control such as the PAUSE / MENU button makes the return deterministic; otherwise focus falls to <body>.

PlainPortfolio's root is `<div class="cx cx--light pp">` containing the skip link, <header>, `<main id="plain-portfolio" tabIndex={-1}>` and <footer> as siblings. Hide or inert the wrapper, not just the <main>; GameRoot's `plainPageRoot()` already climbs to it.
The name heading level is one constant, `NAME_HEADING_LEVEL` in PlainPortfolio.tsx, or the `nameHeadingLevel` prop. It defaults to <h1>; pass 2 if the title screen keeps its own <h1>.
The `actions` slot sits at the right of the sticky header. Below 520 px the brand name is hidden and a `.btn-retro` in the slot is shrunk, so keep it to one compact button.
Overlay and plain page can be in the DOM together: element ids are namespaced by variant (`cx-overlay-…`, `cx-plain-…`, `pp-…`).
The overlay is `position: fixed; z-index: 40`. The flash layer should sit above it.

The contact form needs no `emailjs.init`: it dynamically imports emailjs-com on first submit and passes the public key explicitly. `ContactTransportContext` (exported from sections/ContactForm.tsx) swaps the delivery for tests; both harness pages always provide a mock.

CSS: CourseOverlay imports course.css; PlainPortfolio imports course.css and plain.css. Both depend on the tokens in globals.css and on `--font-outfit`, `--font-titan` and `--font-pixel-face` being set on <html>.

The hero photo in PlainPortfolio uses next/image with `priority`. If the plain page is in the DOM but hidden behind the game at first paint, that preload competes slightly with the title screen; drop `priority` there if that matters.
The harness pages live under /dev and 404 in production through the existing dev layout. /dev/plain is a server component on purpose.

review.summary:
I reviewed the course overlays and the plain HTML version on the live dev server at localhost:3000, which is up again. The builder's report said this code had only been checked outside Next. The module holds up well: all six overlays and the plain page look polished at desktop, mobile, 320 px and landscape phone sizes. The page driver showed no page or console errors. Type-check is clean and the builder's own test suite passes live (99 passed, 0 failed). The WCAG contrast check flagged 0 of 533 text elements. I found and fixed three real problems.
1. Focus did not come back after closing an overlay in the game. The HUD (heads-up display: the lobby's on-screen buttons) is disabled until the jump-out animation finishes, so the one attempt to move focus back on close always failed. The documented `data-overlay-return-focus` hook was effectively broken as a result. It now retries for a few seconds.
2. Opening a Star Mission with Enter or Space on a phone-width screen scrolled the focused tab out of view.
3. On the plain page at phone and tablet widths, links to `#projects` and other anchors landed with the heading under the sticky header. The section nav there also scrolls sideways with no hint that more links exist.
One item fails and is outside my files: the content file names a Nintendo character ("Piranha Plant").
requirementChecks: PASS: Shared section components render from src/content/portfolio.ts with variant overlay|plain: education, skills, career, certifications, about/contact, résumé card. No invented facts in module-authored strings; the labels (Milestones, Career focus, Bonus star, Résumé unlocked!, and so on) are non-factual.
PASS: Education shows degree, institution, status, location, milestones and selectable coursework cards. These are real tabs with arrow keys, Home/End and roving tabindex, verified live.
PASS: Skills are shown as categorized inventory grids (5 groups with item counts).

FIXED: Career Star Missions: 5 clickable tabs, each with objective, tools and outcome, and Star 3 shows both jobs; ?mission= preselects a mission. Keyboard activation no longer scrolls the focused tab out of view on stacked layouts.

PASS: Certifications: extruded CSS 3D gold star for completed ones, outlined badge for in-progress ones, plus issuer, date (where present), competencies and status. The verification link appears only when verifyUrl exists (none do). Reduced motion pauses the stars at a three-quarter angle; checked computed styles and rm-certs.png.

PASS: About & Contact: bio, career focus, email, phone, LinkedIn, GitHub, the résumé-star download (the PDF returns 200 application/pdf) and the contact form. The form uses emailjs-com sendForm, imported lazily. With the mock transport: validation, the Sending… state, success and failure all pass. Real EmailJS delivery was not exercised.
PASS: Résumé star overlay is a compact card with the PDF button and contact links; exit button reads [ BACK TO THE LOBBY (ESC) ].

PASS: CourseOverlay dialog: role=dialog with aria-modal and aria-labelledby; focus moves to the h2; Tab and Shift+Tab are trapped; focus that escapes is pulled back. Esc calls onExit exactly once, also inside GameRoot (/dev/ui?state=course gives exitCourse() once and no pause). The exit button reads [ JUMP OUT OF PAINTING (ESC) ] and is at least 44 px at every tested size.

FIXED: Focus return after close. The game HUD is inert during the exit sequence, so the old single focus() call never worked in-game. It now retries every 100 ms for up to 4 s and stops as soon as anything else takes focus. Verified that an element marked data-overlay-return-focus gets focus once the lobby is back.
PASS: Typing in the overlay contact form inside GameRoot with the real engine is not taken over by game keys (W, M, Space, arrows): the textarea value was correct and mute was not toggled.

PASS: PlainPortfolio is server-renderable (/dev/plain is a server component). It has main#plain-portfolio and the legacy anchors #home #about #education #skills #experience #projects #certification #contact, a single h1, no skipped heading levels, and everything shown in the browser is present in the server HTML.

FIXED: Plain page anchor offset at 1023 px and below. The header is about 111 px but the scroll margin was 108 px. Added a fade on the trailing edge of the sideways-scrolling mobile nav, with end padding so the last link (Contact) clears the fade.

PASS: Every content string is reachable: 298 of 311 rendered in both overlays and plain page. The 13 not shown are internal ids, the 3 EmailJS ids, and the success/failure messages that only appear after a submit.
PASS: Contrast audit: 533 text elements, 0 below WCAG AA.

FAIL (outside module files): The content file's missions[4].outcome contains the Nintendo character name 'Piranha Plant' and the module renders it verbatim. The content owner needs to reword it; I did not edit portfolio.ts.
issuesFixed: src/components/course/CourseOverlay.tsx: focus return on close was a single focus() call that silently failed whenever the target was inert, which is always the case in-game during the exit sequence. Added a tryFocus helper that checks the target is connected and rendered and confirms focus actually landed. Now it retries every 100 ms (up to 40 times), stops when anything else takes focus, and skips the retry entirely when there is no opener and no opt-in target. I deliberately did not add a fallback to the HUD pause button: Space is the jump key, and a focused button would take it (tested: Space then opened the pause menu).
src/components/course/sections/MissionTabs.tsx: activating a tab from the keyboard (a click event with detail 0) no longer scrolls the briefing into view on stacked layouts. Tap and click still do.

src/components/course/plain.css: --pp-anchor-offset raised to 8.25rem at 1023 px and below, so anchored headings clear the roughly 111 px sticky header (they were partly under it at 108 px). The mobile section nav now fades out at its trailing edge so it reads as scrollable, and has end padding so the last link scrolls clear of the fade.
issuesRemaining: Content (not my files): src/content/portfolio.ts missions[4].outcome mentions 'Piranha Plant', a Nintendo character name. The content owner should decide whether to reword it.
Real EmailJS delivery has never been exercised (the dev harnesses always use a mock). One manual send is needed before launch.
Header thumbnails still show the stub painting art until the services registry is flipped.

In-game, the HUD becomes inert while a painting is entered, which drops focus to <body>. So the overlay usually has no opener to return focus to. Returning focus in-game needs GameRoot to put data-overlay-return-focus on a persistent control (see integration notes).
integrationNotes: To return keyboard focus after a course closes, GameRoot can add data-overlay-return-focus to a persistent control. CourseOverlay now waits until that control is no longer inert (the end of the exit sequence) and gives up early if anything else takes focus. Choose that target knowing that a focused button takes the Space (jump) key.

With /dev/ui?state=course&engine=real, Esc calls exitCourse() but the real engine stays in phase 'course'. The harness pokes the store directly, so the engine never entered the course itself. This is an observation about the engine and harness, not a course-module issue; with the mock engine, exit works end to end.
PlainPortfolio's hero image uses next/image priority. If the plain page sits hidden behind the game at first paint, consider dropping priority there.
